criteria.no: The statement requires something the speaker did not ask for, such as a chosen algorithm, strength, number, tool, trigger, or policy, or the opposite of what they asked.
criteria.unclear: It cannot be determined whether the speaker asked for a detail the statement requires.
criteria.yes: The speaker asked for what the statement requires; the statement only formalizes, names more precisely, illustrates, or selects one of their directives.

faithful.instructions: Would someone who said `anchor.quote` agree that `anchor.statement` asks for what they asked for, and nothing they did not ask for? Treat a formal rewrite, a more precise naming of the same thing, illustrative test values, or keeping only one of their several directives as agreement. Treat a newly chosen algorithm, strength, number, tool, trigger, or extra policy as something they did not ask for. Do not judge whether the statement is vague.

criteria.no: The requirement is only a quality judgment, an unexplained name or code, or an unrecorded approval.
criteria.unclear: Something inspectable is mentioned, but it does not settle compliance.
criteria.yes: A reviewer could inspect the named output, file, path, value, stream or behavior and get a definite pass or fail.

observable.instructions: Does `anchor.statement` say what a reviewer would look at to confirm compliance: a command's output, a file or path, a value, a stream, or a behavior under a stated condition? Answer no when the only thing required is a quality judgment (for example 'robust'), conformance to an unexplained name or code, or someone's say-so that leaves no record.

criteria.no: No subject is named; the requirement applies to nothing identifiable.
criteria.unclear: A subject is hinted at but cannot be identified.
criteria.yes: A subject (component, artifact, process, path, or explicit set) is named.

scoped.instructions: Does `anchor.statement` or `anchor.scope` name the subject the requirement applies to, such as a command, module, service, pipeline, artifact, process, path, or an explicit 'all' or 'every' set? A named subject is enough even when the requirement about it is vague or poorly worded.

criteria.no: Applying it needs outside knowledge: the meaning of a subjective quality, an unexplained label or code, or an unrecorded approval.
criteria.unclear: It is unclear whether some term needs outside knowledge.
criteria.yes: No outside knowledge is needed; the statement uses common technical vocabulary and concrete content only.

self_contained.instructions: Does applying `anchor.statement` require knowledge that is not in the statement itself? Answer yes when nothing outside is needed. Common technical vocabulary (commands, paths, flags, formats, streams, environment variables, named tools) is not outside knowledge. A subjective quality word, an unexplained label or requirement code, or a person's approval that is not recorded anywhere is outside knowledge.

criteria.no: It joins separate obligations, such as different actions or different subjects, that can pass or fail independently.
criteria.unclear: It cannot be told whether the parts are one behavior or separate obligations.
criteria.yes: All parts describe one required behavior or prohibition, including its trigger and every surface it applies to.

single_constraint.instructions: Imagine checking `anchor.statement` with pass/fail tests. Would every part of the statement be settled by checking one required behavior, or does the statement join separate obligations that would each need their own check because one can pass while the other fails? Listing several outputs, files, streams or conditions for the same behavior is still one behavior. Ignore whether the statement is vague, faithful to the quote, or scoped.

anchor.statement: The service must retry failed requests twice.
anchor.quote: The service must log requests as JSON and retry failed requests twice.
